name: Ferdinand Marcos Jr
_note: M2 benchmark expansion: President of the Philippines since 30 June 2022. International benchmark (reference head of government), not part of the ranked Malaysian class. C1 (coalition pivotality) and C2 (governance index) are jurisdiction-specific structural dimensions and are left unrecorded for this reference point rather than imputed without the chamber's seat math; the benchmark anchors the conduct (Layer B) and integrity (A5) scales. metrics.justification: Factual status only, not a verdict on severity. Personal criminal conviction of record: convicted 27 Jul 1995 for failure to file income-tax returns (1982-1985, as an Ilocos Norte official), affirmed by the Court of Appeals (a fine, no imprisonment), made final when his Supreme Court appeal was withdrawn in Aug 2001. The Election Commission ruled (20 Apr 2022) it did not disqualify him from office. The separate Marcos estate-tax liability (assessment final and executory in 1999, still unpaid) is an estate matter, not his personal criminal conviction.

citation.title: Candidate Marcos Jr. clears big legal obstacle (1995 tax conviction, COMELEC ruling)

metrics.justification: Handled the West Philippine Sea standoffs with a firm posture (declared the Philippines "cannot yield," 22 Jul 2024) while reaching a provisional resupply arrangement with China for Second Thomas Shoal, easing the acute flashpoint without conceding the claim; the 2024 typhoon cluster drew criticism over disaster gaps as a state of calamity was declared and relief released. Decisive on some fronts, mixed outcomes (anchor 2).

citation.title: Marcos says Philippines 'cannot yield' in South China Sea dispute

metrics.justification: Enacted two championed reforms into operative law: the Maharlika Investment Fund Act (signed 18 Jul 2023, the country's first sovereign wealth fund) and the CREATE MORE Act cutting corporate tax for registered enterprises (signed 11 Nov 2024); but his signature P20-per-kilo rice pledge was materially diluted to a targeted subsidy programme rather than a market price. Reforms delivered, headline pledge diluted (anchor 3).

citation.title: PBBM signs Maharlika Investment Fund Act, PH's first-ever sovereign wealth fund

metrics.justification: His government executed the ICC arrest warrant against predecessor Rodrigo Duterte, surrendering him to the court on 12 Mar 2025, and the impeachment of Vice-President Sara Duterte ran through constitutional process (and was checked by the Supreme Court). But the Duterte split is a partisan power struggle rather than consensus-building, and he declined to rejoin the Rome Statute or abolish the red-tagging task force. Mixed: one accountability-enabling act against capture concerns (anchor 2).

citation.title: Situation in the Philippines: Rodrigo Roa Duterte in ICC custody

metrics.justification: In his 22 Jul 2024 state-of-the-nation address he acknowledged on the record that rice at P45-65/kg meant ordinary Filipinos did not feel economic gains, and the administration downgraded the P20 pledge to a subsidised programme; but he later re-spun the target as still "possible," reframing rather than cleanly owning the abandonment. Reversal acknowledged then re-spun (anchor 2).
